name: riichiprac 2.5D shell baker
status: Phase 3.5 (2026-11-16): adds the per-shell contact-shadow decals (frontend/public/table/overlays.json, baked by tools/render/scripts/bake_overlays.mjs) for the tile-to-tile slivers the group blob cannot reach. The 107-shell catalogue, the base scale, the cameras and the group-shadow contract are unchanged. Phase 3b (2026-11-16): the twelve-shell base adds the left/right standing blue-back hand shells, one per side and reused down a single row; the 107-shell catalogue is otherwise the Phase 1c/1d/2/2b bake. The surface/side hand shells are bare, use the side-wall off-axis camera, and carry a wider standing shadow box. Phase 1c refinement: per-slot front/back walls, per-slot standing hand, standing top hand and the darker silhouette-following shadow. The base scale, the eight-shell base catalogue, the 2-tile wall stack, the face-up dora shells and the side-wall lateral perspective are unchanged. The human hand is a 13-tile row plus a separate drawn-tile slot; the top hand is a dedicated 13-slot standing blue-back fan. Ponds and melds stay straight-on (azimuth 0) with four glyph orientations. The contact shadow is darker (peak 0.22) and follows the tile silhouette inside the body box, so the beveled corners are shadowed; its shape/falloff is the open calibration. Phase 2 landed the 37 face glyphs and the 16-shell startup atlas; layout and renderer are later phases.

paint.material: flat face paint (runtime 2D glyphs; also the carved decal paint)

stack.note: A wall column is a stack of two tiles built from the same single shell perspective (Tenhou-style: the perspective does not change down the column even though it physically would). The bottom tier is a face-down wall shell; the top tier is the same shell offset by the published stackStepPx, or the face-up dora shell for a revealed indicator. The stack step is the projected thickness (straight up), not the face grid step.

lighting.convention: World axes: +X is screen right, -Y is toward the viewer/human edge, +Z is up off the felt. The key is one virtual light locked to screen-space top-left-front: its reference vector is authored for a front-elevation camera (azimuth 0 fronts -Y, 90 is +X, 180 is +Y, 270 is -X; elevation is above horizontal) and is then re-expressed in each shell camera's own basis (screen right, screen up, toward viewer) every time the camera moves. Highlights therefore land on the top/left of the sprite and shadows on the bottom/right in every projection, including the top-down and oblique ones.
lighting.status: Phase 1 bake. The screen-space remap is what makes one key work for six different cameras.

baseScale.note: Phase 1b decision: the Phase 1 @2x output is the new @1x base. The long axis of the projected tile body is now 104 CSS px at @1x (was 52) and 208 px at @2x, so the board coordinate space doubles in both axes and every consumer must read the new shells.json. Render real pixels at the new resolution; never upscale the Phase 1 textures. The shadow is now a synthetic blob with its own padding and sprite, so the old right/bottom shadow and top/left AO pixel contract no longer applies.

shadow.note: A synthetic blob. Every tile gets a rounded rectangle: a lying/upright tile's matches the body's long/short sides (rectScale x the body box plus rectPaddingPx1x), and a standing tile's is fitted to its projected base strip and rotated with the base's principal axes. The corner radius is cornerRadiusFraction x the short half-axis. The shape is filled at core alpha 0.60 and blurred with a separable Gaussian (sigma 12 px @1x lying, 5 px standing). No catcher.

bake.note: One render of the tile on transparent film per scale; there is no shadow-catcher pass. The shadow is a synthetic blob generated in Python from the tile's projected table-contact footprint. Body and shadow are separate sprites, and the runtime/review pass unions the shadows before drawing the bodies.

shadowContract.note: Phase 1d: the shadow is a synthetic translucent-black blob, not a Cycles catcher. A lying/upright tile gets a rounded rectangle matching the body's long/short sides: rectScale x the body box, plus rectPaddingPx1x, with a corner radius of cornerRadiusFraction x the short half-axis. The top edge is then trimmed by topTrimPx1x while the bottom/left/right edges stay fixed, so the shadow does not spill above the tile (light from above/behind). A standing tile gets the same rounded rectangle fitted to its projected base strip (standingRectScale, standingRectPaddingPx1x, standingCornerRadiusFraction) and rotated with the base's axes. The shape is filled at core alpha 0.60 and blurred with a separable Gaussian (sigma 12 px for lying, 5 px for standing). The baker publishes the hard shape as shadowShape; the group recipe draws every placed tile's shape at alpha 1, blurs the union once, and fills it at core alpha. The per-shell sprite is that shape rendered alone. The body carries the tile only.

faceVariants.status: Landed 2026-11-15 for the three landed families: standing-front-00..12 + draw (14 hand slots), flat-topdown (shell_flat_upright) and flat-rot90 (shell_flat_sideways). The 37 glyph masters and the startup atlas are committed; see the architecture doc §11 and tools/render/README.md. The per-slot dora families below remain the next face-variant task.
faceVariants.note: A variant id names the decal's perspective slot, not a camera angle. The face-up dora shells are the top tier of a wall stack, so their decals are their own perspective slots even where the projection matches a pond shell. Face-down wall shells are bare and contribute no atlas entries. The per-slot front/back dora shells are 34 further perspective slots (slotDora); the 14 hand slots are 14 more (handSlots).

slotDora.note: The 17 front + 17 back face-up slot shells are their own atlas keys: each slot is a different perspective, so the dora blank cannot reuse one decal. That is 34 face-up dora shells x 37 faces = 1,258 sprites in addition to the hand/pond/sideway variants; Phase 2 must measure the packed atlas against the committed-asset budget before building it.

handSlots.note: The 14 hand slots are 14 atlas keys: each slot is a different perspective, so the standing hand cannot reuse one decal. 14 x 37 = 518 sprites.

topHand.note: The 13 top-hand slots are standing blue-back shells, bare: no glyph and no face-up atlas keys. They are the human hand's pose turned around, not the flat back-wall shells.

faceVariants.straightOn: Ponds and melds keep the existing flat-topdown / flat-rot90 face variants; the four seats are glyph rotations, not camera slots.

overlay.status: Phase 3.5 follow-up (2026-11-16): contact-ao-band decals, enabled only for the human hand fan (overlay.enabledFamilies). Bands are baked from the committed body alpha, clipped by the compositor to the neighbour's bodyQuads polygon, and drawn between bodies. The face-up lying ponds/melds, top hand, side hands and walls are disabled because the bands read as smudges; the hand's right casts use a side override (sigma 2.5 / alpha 0.50) because the right half looked too wide at the left half's 4 / 0.35.
overlay.sidesNote: Generated by `cd frontend && npm run overlays:export -- --sides` over every layout the engine supports; the baker bakes exactly this set.
overlay.aliases: Shells whose drawn body geometry is identical share a decal; the `_faceup` wall dora shells alias to their face-down twin.
overlay.verification: bake_overlays.mjs refuses a side the layout never asks for; check-overlays.mjs asserts the decoded alpha, the empty outer ring, the zero alpha inside the contour and the zero-on-felt composition.
overlay.enabledNote: Phase 3.5 follow-up (2026-11-16): only the human hand fan is active. The lying face-up ponds/melds looked smudged and are unchanged; remove a family prefix from this list to re-enable it (and re-bake).

right.note: The right half of the hand looked too wide; thinner and darker to match the left half.

budgets.note: The per-slot front/back wall fan, the per-slot hand fan, the separate body/shadow sprites and the larger diffuse rounded-rectangle shadow (sigma 12 px) multiply the catalogue (107 shells, each with a body and a shadow PNG at both scales). The committed shell budget is 6 MiB and the manifest budget 600 KiB (raised from 512 KiB when the per-shell `shadowShape` was added; it is the input that replaces the per-shell shadow sprite dependency for groups); a board loads only the slots it draws, and the total committed asset budget is still 8 MiB with an initial hand + board load under 4 MiB.

wallSlots.note: The front/back walls are a fan of per-slot perspectives, not one shell. The tile directly in front of the human (slot 8 of 17) is straight on. Every other slot is seen from the human's eye, so the far-right tile shows its left side and the far-left tile shows its right side. The camera is the same off-axis perspective as the side walls; only its lateral offset and distance change. front = the bottom wall nearest the human; back = the top wall across the table. A slot's lateral offset is -(index - centreIndex) * stepUnits, i.e. the camera sits at the human's x on the centre line. The face-down and face-up dora shells share the slot's geometry; the back dora's glyph is rotated 180 so it reads for the far player.

front.note: The bottom wall, 40.8 units from the viewer's eye (eye at y -47.8, wall centre at y -7.0 on the 28 mm tile scale). The outer slot sees its tile at 8.4 deg, so the inner long side is visible.

back.note: The top wall, 54.8 units from the viewer's eye (eye at y -47.8, wall centre at y +7.0). The same fan is weaker: the outer slot sees its tile at 6.3 deg.

handSlots.note: The human's standing hand is a per-slot fan, not one shell. The 13 concealed tiles are centred on the player: slot 06 is straight on, slots 00/12 are the outer ends. The drawn tile sits to the right of the 13-tile row with the Phase 3 +0.35 advance gap and gets its own slot. The camera is the player's eye at the centre line: lateralOffsetUnits = -offsetUnits, and the tile is never rotated (rotX 90, rotZ 0). The hand is at a fixed 28 deg elevation; the distance is a stylised eye distance, not the physical seat distance, because the hand must stay readable. The committed distance is 24 units (outer row 10.6 deg, drawn tile 12.9 deg).
handSlots.drawNote: The drawn tile's centre is +5.5125 units from the hand centre: the 13th tile's right edge at +4.875 plus the +0.35 x 0.75 advance gap. The runtime maps a 13-tile hand to the row slots and a 14-tile hand to the row slots plus the draw slot; a shorter hand uses the middle slots and the nearest offset.

topHand.note: The top player's concealed hand is a 13-tile row of standing tiles showing their blue backs, like the human hand turned around. Each slot has its own camera offset from the human's eye at the top-hand distance. The tiles are never laid down: rotX 90 stands them up and rotZ 180 turns the face away, so the camera sees the blue back. The shells are bare (no glyph) and face-down.

straightOn.note: The discard ponds and calls/melds stay straight-on: one shell per body orientation (shell_flat_upright, shell_flat_sideways) with azimuth 0, no per-slot camera. The four seats are four glyph orientations handled by the face variants/glyph rotation, not four camera variants. Confirmed 2026-11-14; refine in a later task.

shadowAudition.status: Calibration only: blob softness, opacity and offset. The committed shadow is REF (sigma 4 px, core 0.60, offset 5/7); A/B/C vary it. Written under build/ (gitignored); the committed assets are never touched.
shadowAudition.deliverable: One labelled sheet with a REF row and three candidate rows. Each row shows a six-tile flat discard run plus an isolated tile, a two-tier wall stack, and a six-tile hand run plus an isolated tile, with the blob parameters and the measured seam/isolated luma printed.
